review_candidates.description: This position accepts candidates based in Cambodia, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore and reports to the Vice President, Asia Pacific Programs. It is only open to candidates who reside in the countries mentioned and have or can secure the right to work in these countries. Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50% and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. IJM is seeking a Project Specialist, Forced Criminality who will work with the Vice President, Regional Programs, APAC, IJM teams around the world, and key external stakeholders to strengthen IJM programs to protect people in poverty from violence. The Project Specialist focuses on accelerating protection impact in APAC by leveraging momentum and political will to address forced scamming to drive justice system strengthening needed to address FLS in all sectors. To this end, the Project Specialist provides analysis, guidance, and technical support to APAC program teams in casework, capacity development, survivor leadership and advocacy interventions related to trafficking in persons for forced criminality (TIP-FC). The Project Specialist also provides leadership and technical guidance to IJM partnerships and APAC regional grant funded projects addressing forced criminality. The Project Specialist contributes to IJM Global, Regional and Advancement Office teams’ efforts to drive improvements in global responses to trafficking in persons while strengthening IJM's credibility, reputation and brand as a standard setting practitioner and thought leader. This includes providing briefings and analysis products to colleagues and partners on trends and effective responses to TIP-FC, strategic media engagements, and representing IJM through speaking and appearances in public forums at global, regional and country levels. Responsibilities Strategic and technical leadership in TIP-FC, enabling IJM Programs to strengthen the design, implementation, monitoring, and adaptive management of strategies and discreet interventions to achieve country project goals by addressing trafficking in persons for forced criminality (TIP-FC). Provide strategic advice to APAC regional leaders, country projects and their partners on emerging TIP-FC trends, typologies, recruitment methods, regional trafficking dynamics, and government and private sector responses. The Project Specialist will ensure that grant-funded project designs and activities, awareness campaigns, stakeholder engagement strategies, and learning products are informed by emerging trends, survivor experiences, evidence-based practices, and international standards on TIP-FC. Technical guidance and recommendations for implementation of projects to ensure alignment with IJM and donor priorities and applicable grant project objectives. Research, Analysis, and Knowledge Management - trend analysis and technical guidance for IJM teams and partners on TIP-FC. Technical contributions to learning events, stakeholder consultations, evaluations, studies, and research initiatives. Support the interpretation of monitoring and evaluation findings and recommend programmatic adjustments. Ensure that learning about TIP-FC from survivor experiences, evaluations, and emerging evidence is integrated into project implementation and strategic planning. Media Engagement and Communications Support for IJM teams, and grant projects and partners. Support development of messaging and communication materials related to TIP-FC to ensure accuracy, survivor sensitivity, relevance to evolving trends, and fitness for purpose. Provide expert input into public information campaigns targeting source and destination countries, advising on high-risk populations, recruitment trends, and prevention messaging strategies. Strengthen the familiarity of project staff, government counterparts, journalists, civil society organizations, and private-sector actors on TIP-FC concepts and responses. In consultation with IJM Regional and County Office leadership and communications and media staff, represent IJM in interviews with journalists, other media engagements, and public speaking opportunities to increase IJM’s credibility and influence, and to advance IJM advocacy goals. Capacity Development and Stakeholder Support directed at IJM implementing partners, and key government, private sector and civil society stakeholders. Manage project and communications engagement outcomes for program analysis and monitoring and evaluation. Design and deliver technical trainings, webinars, workshops, and presentations for partners and stakeholders. Participate in regional forums, consultations, and learning events as a technical resource person. Contribute to strengthening private-sector understanding of the relationship between cyber scams, organized crime, and trafficking in persons. Advise on the development of training/presentation materials, guidance notes, and tools for financial institutions, telecommunications companies, technology companies, and other private-sector stakeholders. Support engagement with social media platforms, job search platforms, and technology companies to improve detection and removal of trafficking-related recruitment advertisements. Review and advise on data-driven approaches to identifying online recruitment patterns linked to forced criminality. Supervisory Reports to the Vice President, Regional Programs, Asia Pacific Does not directly supervise other staff; may supervise consultants or contract staff from time to time. Education & Experience Advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in Criminology, Law, Human Rights, International Development, International Relations, Public Policy, Sociology, Psychology, or a related field; a bachelor's degree combined with significant relevant experience may be considered in lieu of an advanced degree. Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in anti-trafficking programming, transnational organized crime, migration, victim protection, law enforcement cooperation, or related fields. Demonstrated expertise in Trafficking in Persons (TIP), particularly for forced criminality, cyber scam center trafficking, labor trafficking, online-facilitated recruitment, and transnational crime networks. Experience working in Southeast Asia and familiarity with TIP dynamics, migration routes, and regional anti-trafficking mechanisms. Proven experience providing technical leadership to multi-stakeholder initiatives involving governments, international organizations, civil society, and private-sector actors. Experience conducting research, trend analysis, policy analysis, and developing technical guidance documents related to human trafficking and organized crime. Demonstrated experience supporting donor-funded projects, preferably funded by the U.S. Government, United Nations agencies, or other international donors. Excellent writing and verbal communication skills. Strong program development and management skills. Proven ability to lead cross-culturally to set and achieve significant outcomes and impact. Proven ability to lead initiatives in a matrix reporting structure. Proven ability to deliver regional programs funded by multiple donors with different priorities. Critical Qualities Demonstrated ability to appropriately handle stress and conflict. Excellent negotiation and influencing skills. Courageous, confident and servant leadership. Sound and disciplined in judgment and problem solving. Rigorously result-oriented. Resilient; persevering in joy through challenge and failure. Application Process Please submit your Resume/CV and Cover Letter to apac_recruiting@ijm.org no later than 4 December 2026 . Remarks: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assess the candidates value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes. IJM requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.

review_candidates.title: Junior Market Advisor
review_candidates.description: Are you commercially driven, fast moving and motivated by winning and delivering projects for your own clients? Do you have experience from management consulting or business development, and want to help Norwegian companies succeed in Spain and Portugal? Take this opportunity to join our team in Madrid! We are now looking to hire a Junior Market Advisor for the Innovation Norway office in Madrid, covering Spain and Portugal. We are a dedicated team of market advisors who support Norwegian companies with market entry and expansion, trade promotion and tourism, working closely with the Norwegian Embassy in Madrid and Portugal and the wider Team Norway. We offer a flexible, dynamic and supportive work environment, built on trust and meaningful work with a strong purpose. You will work in a flat, collaborative culture with real responsibility from day one. You will work closely with Norwegian companies, Spanish and Portuguese partners, public stakeholders and Innovation Norway's global network of offices. We offer competitive compensation and a good balance between work and private life to support long term performance. The office mainly follows the Norwegian holiday calendar, with some flexibility when client work allows. About The Role This is a hands on, commercial advisor role. You will have your own portfolio of Norwegian clients and be responsible for the full cycle: identifying opportunities, selling consultancy projects, and delivering them with high quality and speed. Your performance will be measured primarily on billable hours, so we are looking for someone who enjoys working with clear targets and takes ownership of reaching them. The role also includes a limited number of hours each month dedicated to administration and IT tasks for the office. The position is based in Madrid and is a local position with local employment terms and conditions. , Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: Sales and Client Development: Building and growing your own client portfolio by identifying Norwegian companies with potential in Spain and Portugal, running sales meetings, and turning leads into signed consultancy agreements with clear deliverables and pricing. Advisory Delivery: Scoping and delivering paid consultancy projects for your clients, including market analysis, partner and distributor search, meeting programmes and stakeholder mapping. You will be the main point of contact for your clients and responsible for results, timelines and billing. Business Promotion and Events: Contributing to our one to many events, such as the Norwegian Pavilion at Seafood Processing Global in Barcelona, FITUR in Madrid and trade missions across Spain and Portugal, and using them actively to generate new clients and projects. Administration and IT: Handling a limited number of administration and IT tasks each month in cooperation with the Country Director and the team. You will also work with colleagues across Europe and in Norway, and the position involves some travel in Spain and Portugal. , Please apply with your CV (no more than 2 pages) and a motivation letter in English. For questions about the position, contact Country Director Karin Greve-Isdahl at karin.greve-isdahl@innovationnorway.no. Application deadline: as fast as possible and no later that 26th November 2026. Innovation Norway seeks employees with different competencies, perspectives, ages, genders, and life experiences. Diversity is important both for our working environment and for the work we are set to do. Innovation Norway carry out background checks on relevant candidates to verify documents/information and assess security related matters. Relevant candidates will receive additional information about this. Furthermore, applicants must be prepared to provide information about any ties to high risk countries as part of a security assessment. , Around 3 years of experience from management consulting, business development or sales in the private sector. A proven track record of selling and delivering advisory services or B2B projects, preferably to international clients. Strong skills in PowerPoint, Excel and Copilot. Ability to build partnerships with both public and private sector stakeholders. Strong organisational skills and experience handling several clients and deliveries at the same time. A higher academic degree, preferably in business or economics. Fluent in Spanish and English, written and spoken. Portuguese and/or a Scandinavian language is an added advantage. A strong interest in trade promotion, business development and internationalisation. Core competencies and collaborative skills: Commercially minded, with drive to find and close new business. Fast and efficient, able to move from idea to delivery quickly. Take ownership of your clients, targets and results. Strong interpersonal skills and a positive, proactive attitude. Comfortable sharing your advice and ideas with clients and colleagues. Commitment, honesty and accountability in all tasks.

review_candidates.title: Investigations & Law Enforcement Development Specialist, Malaysia
review_candidates.description: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, we are seeking an Investigation & Law Enforcement Development Specialist to support implementation of IJM Malaysia’s Investigations and Law Enforcement Development (ILED) strategy by providing sustained operational engagement with law enforcement, investigation and intelligence support, proactive case development, case progression, and capacity development focused on trafficking in persons and forced labour. Working closely with the ILED Manager and IJM’s Casework, Legal, Aftercare and Program teams, the specialist strengthens case quality, victim identification, evidence development, inter-agency coordination and accountability outcomes while building trusted professional relationships with Malaysian justice-sector partners. The specialist generates field-level information, intelligence, case insights and operational analysis to inform strategic decisions led by the ILED Manager and is expected to operate with professional discretion, sound investigative judgment, a survivor-centered and trauma-informed approach, and a strong understanding of the Malaysian law enforcement environment. This position is based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia and reports to Law Enforcement Development Manager, Malaysia and is only available for candidates with the right to work in Malaysia. Responsibilities Casework Proactively identify, assess and develop promising trafficking and forced labour case opportunities through lawful intelligence gathering, stakeholder engagement, referrals, open-source information and analysis; develop well-supported leads and case-development recommendations for assessment and prioritization by the ILED Manager; Provide hands-on investigation and intelligence support for IJM-supported trafficking and forced labour matters, including evidence review, investigative gap analysis, development of investigative hypotheses, OSINT, information assessment and preparation of operational recommendations; Support victim and witness engagement, interviews and referrals in coordination with appropriate IJM teams and government partners, applying trauma-informed, survivor-centered and culturally appropriate practices; Follow up on agreed investigative actions and case-development steps to maintain momentum throughout the lifecycle of priority cases. Fieldwork Projects Participate in approved field-based investigative and case-support activities, including joint field visits, victim identification activities, stakeholder meetings, and engagement with law enforcement, prosecutors and other justice-sector partners as appropriate; Travel throughout Malaysia as required to support priority casework and law enforcement engagement, documenting relevant observations, risks and recommended follow-up actions. Networking & Partnership Build and maintain trusted professional relationships with investigators, operational leaders and focal points within RMP/PDRM, JIM, MAPO, JTKSM, AGC and other relevant government or civil-society partners; Facilitate authorized communication, case conferences, referrals, information sharing and coordination among IJM and external stakeholders to support victim identification, investigation progression and prosecution readiness; Track relevant agency structures, focal points and personnel changes to preserve continuity of engagement and reduce disruption to priority investigations; Support cross-border coordination and information exchange with IJM regional offices and approved international partners when cases involve transnational recruitment, movement, exploitation or repatriation. Research, Program Management and M&E Analyze casework, partner-engagement and trafficking-trend information to identify emerging patterns, recurring risks and operational implications relevant to ILED casework and partner support; Contribute operational data and analysis to case reviews, program monitoring and learning, including identification of progress, risks, lessons and recommended follow-up actions. Training and Development Support the design and delivery of practical training, mentoring, workshops and technical consultations for law enforcement, immigration, labour and other justice-sector partners on victim identification, investigative methods, evidence development, interviewing and inter-agency coordination; Provide case-based coaching during active matters and identify recurring capability gaps that should inform future ILED capacity-development initiatives; Contribute to the development and adaptation of practical tools, guidance and protocols that support sustainable improvements in trafficking and forced labour investigations. Strategy & Knowledge Development & Implementation Maintain a current understanding of relevant Malaysian legal frameworks, agency mandates, investigative procedures and operational practices, and apply this knowledge to support effective ILED casework and law enforcement engagement; Systematically identify and document recurring investigative, operational and coordination bottlenecks encountered by law enforcement partners through casework and partner engagement and provide evidence-based analysis to the ILED Manager to inform technical assistance, intervention design and capacity-development priorities. Documentation, Reporting & Data Management Prepare clear and timely case summaries, intelligence notes, investigation briefs, stakeholder updates and program reports for internal decision-making and approved external engagement; Maintain accurate case and stakeholder records in IJM-approved systems and ensure sensitive information is handled in accordance with confidentiality, safeguarding, security and data-protection requirements; Document and synthesize lessons, emerging trends, investigative patterns and good practices from casework and partner engagement to strengthen IJM Malaysia’s institutional knowledge and casework capability. General tasks Provide routine investigative and operational coordination support arising from active casework and partner engagement, as assigned by the ILED Manager and consistent with the scope and authority of the position. Qualifications Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in law, Criminology, Criminal Justice, Social Sciences or another relevant discipline; Minimum five years of professional experience in criminal investigations, investigative intelligence, law enforcement, prosecution or another operational investigative role; Demonstrated experience supporting criminal investigations, evidence development and investigative interviews with victims, witnesses or persons of interest; Demonstrated experience working directly with law enforcement or justice-sector agencies during active investigations or case progression; Experience in trafficking in persons, forced labour, organized crime, migrant-worker exploitation or related complex investigations is highly desirable; Experience working within the Malaysian law enforcement or criminal justice context and across multiple government agencies is strongly preferred; Willingness and ability to travel regularly throughout Malaysia; Malaysian driving licence or ability to obtain one is preferred. Strong criminal investigation and case-development skills, including evidence assessment, investigative planning, interviewing, intelligence analysis and identification of evidential gaps; Ability to conduct and document OSINT and other lawful information-development activities, assess source credibility and produce concise intelligence or investigation products; Ability to translate investigative findings into practical recommendations for law enforcement coordination, victim protection and prosecution readiness; Experience supporting training, mentoring or technical assistance for law enforcement or other justice-sector practitioners; Strong professional writing and digital literacy, including proficiency with Microsoft Office and case/information management systems; Strong oral and written communication skills in Bahasa Malaysia and English. Critical Qualities High integrity, discretion and sound professional judgment when handling sensitive case, survivor and law enforcement information; Strong investigative mindset, professional curiosity and initiative; able to identify opportunities and problems without waiting for detailed direction; Analytical, organized and results-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain consistent follow-up; Strong interpersonal, networking and relationship-building skills, with diplomacy and cultural sensitivity in multi-agency and cross-cultural environments; Able to work independently with limited supervision while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary teams; Resilient and composed under pressure, receptive to feedback, and able to adapt to changing operational priorities; Demonstrated commitment to survivor-centered, trauma-informed practice and to IJM’s mission, values, safeguarding standards and Code of Ethics. Application Process Please submit your Resume/CV and Cover Letter to IJM@monroeconsulting.com not later than 30 November 2026 . Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assess the candidates value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes.
